question.prompt: A square-shaped floor is covered with congruent square tiles. If the total number of tiles that lie on the two diagonals is \(37,\) how many tiles cover the floor?

solutions.explanation:
Let \(n\) be the positive integer number of tiles along each side. The floor has \(n\) rows of \(n\) tiles, and each diagonal passes through the interiors of \(n\) tiles. Adding the two diagonal counts gives \(2n\), but any tile on both diagonals must be counted only once.

If \(n\) is even, the diagonals meet at a corner of the four middle tiles and share no tile interiors. Their total is then \(2n\), an even number, so it cannot be \(37\).

If \(n\) is odd, both diagonals pass through the central tile, and this is their only shared tile. Therefore
\[
2n-1=37,
\qquad n=\frac{37+1}{2}=19.
\]
There are \(19\) rows with \(19\) tiles in each, so the floor contains
\[
19\times19=\boxed{361}
\]
tiles, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Count the shared central tile once
